primitives.note: Concussive Blows: Braum's basic attacks and Winter's Bite each place a stack (refreshing, cap 4, 4s duration) on the dummy; the 4th stack consumes all stacks to deal burst magic damage and stun.
After the stun triggers, the target is immune to new stacks for a level-gated duration, during which Braum's basic attacks deal +40% bonus magic damage on-hit.
Winter's Bite: magic damage (base + %maxHP) to the dummy on a 0.25s cast, on cooldown.
Glacial Fissure: magic damage (base + 60% AP) to the dummy on a 0.5s cast, on cooldown.
Self-cast Stand Behind Me instantly grants Braum bonus armor and MR (36% of bonus resists) for 3s; relevant only to the survival fight's damage-taken.
Unbreakable grants a facing damage-reduction percent plus a one-time 100% block of the first champion damage instance from that direction; relevant only to the survival fight.
All four abilities cost mana; casting Q/R on cooldown plus any W/E use over a 15s fight is a real mana constraint, though base mana/regen at the tested level/items aren't given in these sheets.

needsBespoke.why: The kit is fully describable with the closed-list primitives: passive stacking-to-consume plus a post-proc conditional on-hit bonus, two plain-cast nukes (Q, R), a timed self-buff (W self-cast) and a pure defensive mechanic (E) that only the survival fight reads, gated by a real mana budget. No extra logic (pets, forms, ammo, crits, stat conversion, etc.) is needed.

unsettled.question: Is the passive's 4th-stack burst damage (and its +40% on-hit follow-up) a distinct 'spell' damage instance that can trigger on-cast/spell-based item and rune effects, or is it folded into whichever attack/spell applied the triggering stack for on-hit purposes?
options: Treated as its own proc damage instance (per flags: spelleffects=Proc, spellshield=True), separate from the attack/spell that applied the 4th stack, so on-hit effects from that attack still apply once and the proc is a second, independent magic-damage event
Bundled with the triggering attack as a single combined damage event for on-hit/on-cast interaction purposes

proposal: Open the 15s window auto-attacking the dummy continuously to start applying Concussive Blows stacks and generate basic-attack damage.
Cast Winter's Bite (Q) as soon as it comes off cooldown each time, both for its own magic damage (base + 2.5% max HP) and because it also applies a Concussive Blows stack.

Let the passive trigger naturally: whenever the 4th stack lands (from an auto or Q), it fires its burst magic damage and stun-flag on the dummy, then Braum's autos deal +40% bonus magic damage during the target's immunity window.

Cast Glacial Fissure (R) once available (its long cooldown means only one cast fits in 15s) for its flat + 60% AP magic damage, timed so the cast (0.5s) doesn't stall auto-attacking/Q-weaving longer than necessary.

Do not cast Stand Behind Me (W) or Unbreakable (E) in the damage fight: both are purely defensive/self-buff and add no damage against a stationary, non-retaliating dummy, so casting them would only waste time and mana that could go to Q/R casts and auto-attacks.

In the survival fight, self-cast W at the opener (or on cooldown) for the self-armor/MR buff, and face Unbreakable (E) toward the attacker to get its facing damage reduction and one-time full block, refreshing E off cooldown.
questions: At the target level/items being simulated, is there enough mana to cast Q on every cooldown plus one R cast across the full 15s without stalling, or does mana starvation change the realistic rotation?

Should Glacial Fissure be cast as the very first action (to front-load its long cooldown and start its AoE damage timer) or held until Concussive Blows stacks are already primed, given its 0.5s cast time delays auto-attacking either way?

Does the simulator model Concussive Blows' 4-stack cap purely from Braum's own attacks/Q in a duel (no allies), and does it correctly track the 4s per-stack refresh window when weaving Q between autos?
